content_sections.heading: About JPPO Dumka फसल रक्षक
content_sections.text: The Office of the Junior Plant Protection Officer (JPPO), Dumka, is on Bhagalpur Road in Dumka, Jharkhand. It is a district office of the Agriculture Division of the Jharkhand Government's Department of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperative. The notice says the Crop Protectors are hired under the Crop Protection Programme scheme (फसल सुरक्षा कार्यक्रम योजना) for the financial year 2026-27. The aim is to run crop protection and plant protection work well at the local level.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: Send the application only by registered post to this address, exactly as printed: कार्यालय, कनीय पौधा संरक्षण पदाधिकारी, दुमका (भागलपुर रोड– दुमका, नियर टाटा शोरूम, दुमका, पिन कोड– 814101). In English, this is the Office of the Junior Plant Protection Officer, Dumka, Bhagalpur Road, Dumka, Near Tata Showroom, Dumka, PIN 814101. Get the application form (आवेदन-पत्र). It is printed with the notice and can also be seen on the Dumka district website, dumka.nic.in, and on the notice board of the JPPO Dumka office. Fill in every column clearly and completely. The form asks for your names in Hindi and English, parents' names, gender, date of birth and age as on 30 September 2026. It also asks for your category (UR/ST/EWS), whether you claim reservation, and the district and block on your local certificate. Fill in your Matric, Intermediate/10+2 and graduation marks and the details of your compulsory 5-day training and any extra training. Then answer whether you can ride a bicycle and climb trees, and add your Aadhaar number, mobile, email and addresses. Paste a recent passport-size photograph that you have signed yourself (self-attested), then sign the declaration with the place and date. Attach self-attested photocopies of the documents listed under Enclosures. Send it by registered post so that it reaches the office between 26 October 2026 and 14 November 2026. For more information, call 9304866088. The office email is [email protected] . FREEJOBALERT DAILY QUIZ Preparing for Govt Exams? content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: There is one Crop Protector post at each of 11 Plant Protection Centres: Dumka, Saraiyahat, Ramgarh, Jama, Jarmundi, Masalia, Shikaripara, Kathikund, Gopikandar, Raneshwar and Nonihat. The category-wise split follows the model reservation roster for Dumka district. You can apply only for the centre in your own block: Dumka centre: local residents of Dumka block Saraiyahat centre: local residents of Saraiyahat block Ramgarh centre: local residents of Ramgarh block Jama centre: local residents of Jama block Nonihat centre: local residents of Jarmundi block Jarmundi centre: local residents of Jarmundi block Masalia centre: local residents of Masalia block Shikaripara centre: local residents of Shikaripara block Kathikund centre: local residents of Kathikund block Gopikandar centre: local residents of Gopikandar block Raneshwar centre: local residents of Raneshwar block At least Matric/Secondary (10th) pass from a recognised educational institution. At least one 5-day training from the Directorate of Agriculture or Horticulture under the Department of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperative. Knowledge of the local language. Ability to ride a bicycle and climb trees. You must be a local resident of the block whose centre you are applying for. Age is counted as on 30 September 2026. Only the date of birth on your Matric marksheet or certificate is accepted. The minimum age is 18 years for every category. The Crop Protector gets a monthly honorarium of Rs. 11851/-. The appointment is for 11 months, or until a regular appointment is made, whichever comes first. The post is paid fully by honorarium or remuneration. It gives no claim to a regular appointment or to permanency in future, and no automatic right to the service benefits of regular government staff. See the official notification for the discipline-specific eligibility of each post.

content_sections.heading: JPPO Dumka फसल रक्षक Job Description
content_sections.text: Spraying pesticides. Raising awareness among farmers and training them. Other work given by the office from time to time.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: You must attach self-attested photocopies of the documents below. If any are missing, the application will be treated as incomplete. Matric/10th certificate and marksheet (compulsory) Intermediate/10+2 certificate and marksheet, if available Graduation certificate and marksheet, if available Certificate for training of at least 05 days Local language certificate, if available (the form also lists an additional language certificate, if any) Valid local certificate issued by the competent authority Caste certificate, where applicable Local resident certificate for Dumka district EWS certificate, where applicable Matric certificate as proof of date of birth Identity card Copy of Aadhaar card (clearly readable) Anyone claiming reservation must attach a caste or category certificate issued by the competent authority in the prescribed format. You do not need to send a character certificate with the application. You must produce it at final selection, document verification or joining, in the format set by the competent authority.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: All applications are first checked for eligibility and required documents. An application is rejected if details are missing, required certificates are not attached, the essential qualification is not met, or the information is false or misleading. Valid applications are then scored out of 100 marks. If your marks are in CGPA or grades, they are turned into a percentage using the conversion formula set by your board or university. No extra marks are given for a postgraduate or higher qualification. No extra marks are given for more than one degree or qualification at the same level. Training length is counted by the full training days written on the certificate. Only training certificates from these bodies are accepted: the Directorate of Agriculture and Horticulture under the Agriculture Department, the Krishi Vigyan Kendras of Birsa Agricultural University, and the ATMA office. If the selection committee thinks it is needed, it may hold a practical test of bicycle riding and tree climbing after the provisional merit list. Original certificates of selected or provisionally selected candidates will be checked before final selection, on a date to be fixed later. The merit list will be prepared category-wise under the reservation rules. The final list will be published on dumka.nic.in and on the office notice board. Centres are allotted first by the block on your local residence certificate and then by the preferences in your form. The final decision rests with JPPO Dumka based on administrative needs, and the allotment may be changed later. Selected candidates must join on the terms set by JPPO Dumka. If you do not join in the given time, your selection ends on its own and the post may be filled from the waiting list.

faq.question: Q1. How many Crop Protector vacancies are in JPPO Dumka Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 11 vacancies: 05 UR, 05 ST and 01 EWS. There is one post at each of 11 Plant Protection Centres in Dumka district.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date for the Dumka Fasal Rakshak application?
faq.answer: Applications are accepted from 26 October 2026 to 14 November 2026. Applications received after the last date will not be accepted.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is required for Crop Protector?
faq.answer: You need at least Matric/Secondary (10th) pass from a recognised institution and at least one 5-day training from the Directorate of Agriculture or Horticulture. You also need knowledge of the local language and the ability to ride a bicycle and climb trees.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for JPPO Dumka Crop Protector?
faq.answer: The minimum age is 18 years. The maximum is 35 years for UR and EWS and 40 years for ST, counted as on 30 September 2026 from the date of birth on the Matric certificate.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary of a Crop Protector in Dumka?
faq.answer: The monthly honorarium is Rs. 11851/-.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply for the Dumka Fasal Rakshak post?
faq.answer: Fill in the application form, attach self-attested copies of the required documents, and send it by registered post. The address is the Office of the Junior Plant Protection Officer, Dumka, Bhagalpur Road, Dumka, Near Tata Showroom, Dumka, PIN 814101.

faq.question: Q7. How will Crop Protectors be selected?
faq.answer: Selection is by a merit list out of 100 marks: up to 60 for academic marks, 10 for being a local resident of the block, and up to 30 for training. Original documents are checked before final selection. A practical test of bicycle riding and tree climbing may be held.

faq.question: Q8. Can I apply for a centre outside my block?
faq.answer: No. Only local residents of a block can apply for that block's centre. Residents of Jarmundi block are eligible for both the Jarmundi and Nonihat centres.

faq.question: Q9. Is the Crop Protector job permanent?
faq.answer: No. It is a temporary job paid by honorarium, for 11 months or until a regular appointment is made, whichever comes first. It gives no claim to a regular appointment or to permanency.

faq.question: Q10. Which training certificates are accepted for Crop Protector?
faq.answer: Only certificates from the Directorate of Agriculture and Horticulture under the Agriculture Department, the Krishi Vigyan Kendras of Birsa Agricultural University, and the ATMA office are accepted.
